# 5. Archetypes {#sec-archetypes}

Certain designs recur when the same pressures meet the same scale and sharing position: a farmer's flock under panels, a prairie strip in a wet draw, a retired irrigated field. These **archetypes** are recurring, transformable patterns rather than an exhaustive typology. They classify how pressures are resolved; hardware taxonomies classify structure. The two can be read together.

Six featured archetypes, ordered from farmstead to region, each carry a documented case, and seven further forms are sketched more briefly.

## What appears at each scale {#sec-by-zone}

If you know roughly how much land is in play, start here. The table gives the forms that recur at each [zone](1-the-scale-transect.qmd#sec-zones), with **featured archetypes in bold** and [further ones](#sec-further-types) in plain text, and each name links to its entry. Arrays mounted on buildings take no ground at all and sit at [A0](1-the-scale-transect.qmd#sec-zones), off the table entirely.

::: {.zone-table}
| Zone | Indicative footprint | Forms that recur here |
|---|---|---|
| **A1 — Farmstead** | under ~1 acre | [**Barnyard Shelter**](#arch-barnyard) |
| **A2 — Field** | ~0.5–8 acres | [**Vegetable Agrivoltaics**](#arch-vegetable) · [**Marginal Land**](#arch-marginal) · [Vertical-Bifacial Cropland](#arch-vertical-bifacial) · [Recharge Enhancement](#arch-recharge) |
| **A3 — Parcel** | ~5–80 acres | [**Solar Prairie Strips**](#arch-prairie-strips) · [**Vegetable Agrivoltaics**](#arch-vegetable) · [**Marginal Land**](#arch-marginal) · [Community-Solar Pollinator](#arch-community-solar) · [Vertical-Bifacial Cropland](#arch-vertical-bifacial) · [Recharge Enhancement](#arch-recharge) · [Linear Infrastructure](#arch-linear) · [Ag-Industrial Microgrid](#arch-microgrid) · [Brightfield](#arch-brightfield) |
| **A4 — Landscape** | ~60–400 acres | [**Regenerative Solar Grazing**](#arch-grazing) · [**Water-Sustainability**](#arch-water) · [Native-Grassland Utility](#arch-native-grassland) · [Vertical-Bifacial Cropland](#arch-vertical-bifacial) · [Linear Infrastructure](#arch-linear) · [Ag-Industrial Microgrid](#arch-microgrid) · [Brightfield](#arch-brightfield) |
| **A5 — Regional** | ~300 acres to 10,000+ | [**Regenerative Solar Grazing**](#arch-grazing) · [**Water-Sustainability**](#arch-water) · [Native-Grassland Utility](#arch-native-grassland) · [Brightfield](#arch-brightfield) |
:::

The crowding at A3 is the [feasible wedge](2-the-sharingsparing-axis.qmd#sec-wedge) in practical form: siting and management latitude overlap there. A listed form has been built at that scale; climate, soil, water, market, and neighbors still decide whether it fits a particular site.

## The six featured archetypes {#sec-featured}

**On the worked cases.** The at-a-glance figures below are indicative, drawn from the worked case and from forms in circulation, not requirements. Each featured archetype carries one real project. Several rest on developer pages, NGO case studies, and extension write-ups rather than peer-reviewed evidence; capacities and areas are as-reported and are traced in [Sources](sources.qmd). They illustrate the *form*. They are not verified performance data, and none of them has been independently audited against the [restorative functions](4-restorative-functions.qmd) it is cited for.


### Barnyard Shelter Solar {#arch-barnyard}


::: {.at-a-glance}
**At a glance**

- **Scale** — A1 · ~10–100 kW · under about an acre
- **Position** — S1–S2 — the farm's own animals keep using the ground beneath
- **Ground layer** — the existing yard or paddock; nothing new to establish
- **Clearance** — enough for stock to walk in and shelter under (the case below: cows)
- **Grid** — behind-the-meter — offsets the parlor, cold store, well pump
- **Watch for** — muck and wear concentrating where the animals crowd into the shade
:::
*Restoration by how it's run*

Barnyard shelter solar places a modest array above the yard or paddock the farm's own animals already use. It provides shade and shelter while offsetting the parlor, cold store, or well pump. The same farmer holds the animals, array, and labor, but the array serves the farm rather than the grid; concentrated shade also concentrates manure and wear.

*Dominant pressures: agricultural production, operations and maintenance. Yielded: generation at scale, since the array is sized to the farm rather than the grid.*

**West Central Research and Outreach Center, Morris, Minnesota**, a University of Minnesota dairy where a 30-kilowatt array was raised over the pasture in 2018 to shade thirty to forty grazing cows and power the milking equipment; the shaded herd ran about a degree cooler and panted less, while the same panels carried the parlor's load, a working demonstration that shelter and generation can sit together on one small farm.

### Vegetable Agrivoltaics {#arch-vegetable}


::: {.at-a-glance}
**At a glance**

- **Scale** — A2–A3 · ~100 kW–3 MW · roughly 1–20 acres
- **Position** — S1 — the food crop continues inside the footprint
- **Ground layer** — shade-tolerant vegetables — greens, tomatoes, peppers
- **Geometry** — clearance for hand and small-equipment work; row spacing set by the crop's light needs, not by packing density
- **Grid** — behind-the-meter to distribution
- **Watch for** — shade past the crop's tolerance, which makes this the most engineering-intensive form here, and the one most sensitive to climate
:::
*Restoration by how it's built*

Vegetable agrivoltaics keeps shade-tolerant food crops growing beneath panels raised and spaced for their light and work needs. Its geometry is tuned to a crop and climate: excess shade cuts yield, while in hot, dry settings it can reduce heat and water stress [@barrongafford2019]. The form succeeds only where the crop still pays.

*Dominant pressures: agricultural production, community acceptance. Yielded: some generation and capital, to the clearance and spacing the crop demands.*

**Jack's Solar Garden, Colorado** — the largest commercial agrivoltaics research site in the country: 1.2 megawatts of tracking panels over four acres where partner farmers grow chard, greens, and tomatoes among the rows, a living laboratory for NREL, Colorado State, and University of Arizona researchers.

### Marginal Land Solar {#arch-marginal}


::: {.at-a-glance}
**At a glance**

- **Scale** — A2–A3 · ~100 kW–3 MW · roughly 1–20 acres
- **Position** — S4 — or S2 where the ground still carries stock
- **Ground layer** — whatever the marginal ground supports: rough grazing where it drains, naturalized or pollinator cover where it does not
- **Geometry** — dictated by the parcel — orientation and layout follow the ground, not the optimum
- **Grid** — behind-meter to distribution; the interconnect run can be long
- **Watch for** — ground that is marginal for farming is often marginal for solar too, meaning ballast on rock, elevation above a floodplain, extra cable
:::
*Restoration by where you site*

Marginal land solar uses the farm's flood-prone corners, rocky headlands, wet remnants, and other ground that no longer pays its way, leaving the better fields alone. Rough grazing or naturalized cover can remain beneath the array. What made the parcel marginal for farming can make it costly for solar too, through rock, flood risk, or a long interconnect, and the income has to clear that.

*Dominant pressures: build cost, since the conditions that made the parcel marginal also make the array dearer. What it is for is the [community & economic function](4-restorative-functions.qmd#sec-fn-community): income from ground that was not paying. Yielded: some generation, since marginal ground is rarely shaped for output.*

**Cozy Cove Farm, Gurley, Alabama** — a llama-and-alpaca farm that set a 50-kilowatt array on a flood-prone corner of riverside pasture, raised about seven feet so the herd grazes and shelters beneath, selling the power to the TVA while the pasture keeps working. *This particular site reads as [S2](2-the-sharingsparing-axis.qmd#sec-positions), not S4: the siting decision was the marginal corner, but production never stopped there, since the herd still grazes beneath the panels. It is the archetype's sharing variant, and the reading rule in §2.1 settles it.*

### Solar Prairie Strips {#arch-prairie-strips}


::: {.at-a-glance}
**At a glance**

- **Scale** — A3 · ~1–10 MW · roughly 5–80 acres
- **Position** — S5 — the strip ground leaves production
- **Ground layer** — deep-rooted native prairie, the mix and width sized to a named hydrologic outcome
- **Geometry** — placement follows the water — contour bands, low draws, wet corners, wetland edges
- **Grid** — distribution; often community solar
- **Watch for** — needs a place where clean water is actually paid for; the logic does not carry to utility scale
:::
*Restoration by where you plant*

Solar prairie strips pair panels with deep-rooted prairie placed where a field sheds water: contours, low draws, wet corners, and wetland edges. The planting slows runoff and holds sediment and nutrients; the array gives it a durable revenue stream. STRIPS research found that converting about a tenth of a field to prairie in the right places can cut soil loss by more than 90% [@schulte2017]. 

*Dominant pressures: restorative goals, community acceptance. Yielded: a little generation, to the prairie.*

**Ramsey Renewable Station, Minnesota** — 3.4 megawatts of solar and storage whose native ground layer is the stormwater system itself: on that sandy soil, DOE's PV-SMaRT modeling found the planting absorbed the 2-, 10-, and 100-year design storms with no detention basins at all.

### Regenerative Solar Grazing {#arch-grazing}


::: {.at-a-glance}
**At a glance**

- **Scale** — A4–A5 · 10 MW and up · from tens of acres to several thousand
- **Position** — S2 — forage production continues, subordinate to the array
- **Ground layer** — managed pasture or forage held under a planned rotation
- **Geometry** — clearance and water points set what class of stock can work beneath; fence and gate topology defines the rotation cells
- **Grid** — sub-transmission to transmission
- **Watch for** — scheduling sovereignty — the plant wants the grass low on its calendar, the shepherd moves stock on the flock's; expect cost parity with mowing, not a saving
:::
*Restoration by how it's run*

Regenerative solar grazing uses a planned flock rotation to manage vegetation, cycle nutrients, and support ground cover beneath a utility-scale array. It is usually a contracted service rather than the landowner's own operation, with fences, gates, clearance, and water points setting the rotation. The plant's mowing calendar and the shepherd's flock calendar must be reconciled. Grazing can reach cost parity with mowing [@mccall2023]; well-managed native understory can also improve soil carbon [@krasner2025].

*Dominant pressures: energy yield, operations and maintenance. Yielded: the farm's own agricultural production, since the grazing is a tenancy rather than the operation.*

**Aurora Solar, Minnesota** — 150 megawatts of generation across sixteen sites whose grounds are kept by thousands of contracted sheep grazing a low pollinator understory:

### Water-Sustainability Solar {#arch-water}


::: {.at-a-glance}
**At a glance**

- **Scale** — A4–A5 · 50 MW and up · hundreds to many thousands of acres
- **Position** — S5 — irrigated production ends, by design
- **Ground layer** — low-water cover; the array itself needs no irrigation
- **Geometry** — the unit of design is the district or aquifer, not the parcel
- **Grid** — transmission
- **Watch for** — only works where the overdraft is measured and governed tightly enough that the saved water stays saved
:::
*Restoration by relieving the water budget*

Water-sustainability solar retires irrigated demand above an overdrawn aquifer [@stid2025]. It is credible only where the overdraft is measured and governance keeps the saved water from being pumped elsewhere [@zwickle2021], preferably on drainage-impaired, salt-affected, or otherwise marginal irrigated ground. Food production is deliberately given up; this is a regional form because the impairment must be regional too.

*Dominant pressures: restorative goals (a water-quantity target), build cost. Yielded: agricultural production, by design.*

**Westlands Solar Park, San Joaquin Valley, California**, part of a plan to convert up to ~136,000 acres of drainage-impaired, previously-irrigated land to solar and storage under California's Sustainable Groundwater Management Act; because the panels use no water, retiring the fields eases the overdraft that irrigated farming had driven [@stid2022]. *Figures are developer- and program-reported; see [Sources](sources.qmd).*

## Archetypes across the SCALE domains {#sec-archetype-domains}

Each featured archetype has a characteristic profile across Communities, Agriculture, Landscapes, and Energy. A dominant pressure moves its domain toward regeneration; a yielded pressure moves it toward depletion; unengaged domains remain mid-scale. The profiles are judgments about forms, not measurements or audits of the named projects.

![**Figure 5.1.** Each featured archetype as a SCALE footprint across the four domains: a domain it regenerates sits toward the center, one it depletes or trades away reaches toward the rim, read from its dominant and yielded pressures. Descriptive profiles, site-conditional, and not a ranking or a score against a limit of sustainability.](../figures/fig_archetype_footprints.svg)

- [**Barnyard Shelter Solar**](#arch-barnyard) (A1 · S1–S2): Agriculture and Communities.
- [**Vegetable Agrivoltaics**](#arch-vegetable) (A2–A3 · S1): Agriculture and Communities, trading Energy.
- [**Marginal Land Solar**](#arch-marginal) (A2–A3 · S4, or S2): Communities and cast-off agricultural ground.
- [**Solar Prairie Strips**](#arch-prairie-strips) (A3 · S5): Landscapes, with some Energy yielded.
- [**Regenerative Solar Grazing**](#arch-grazing) (A4–A5 · S2): Energy and Landscapes; Agriculture as a service.
- [**Water-Sustainability Solar**](#arch-water) (A4–A5 · S5): Landscapes and Energy, with Agriculture deliberately given up.



## Further archetypes in current circulation {#sec-further-types}

Seven more archetypes, sketched rather than fully developed, applying the same language to configurations the featured six do not cover.

Two of them sit at [S3](2-the-sharingsparing-axis.qmd#sec-positions) while carrying rich ecological ground layers: the position records that ordinary ground was given over to the array, and the pollinator planting or restored grassland is a [restorative function](4-restorative-functions.qmd) layered on top of it (§2.1, §4).

### Vertical-Bifacial Cropland Array {#arch-vertical-bifacial}

[A2](1-the-scale-transect.qmd#sec-zones)–[A4](1-the-scale-transect.qmd#sec-zones) · **[S1](2-the-sharingsparing-axis.qmd#sec-positions)** · *[structure-led](1-the-scale-transect.qmd#sec-siting-latitude)*

*Dominant pressures:* [agricultural production](3-design-pressures.qmd#sec-pressures), [energy yield](3-design-pressures.qmd#sec-pressures).
*Yielded:* [build cost](3-design-pressures.qmd#sec-pressures) (frameless glass–glass modules, more posts per watt), land-use density.
*Signature levers:* vertical east–west [module technology](7-terminology.qmd#term-module-technology), bifacial modules, wide (~8 m) row geometry set by machinery rather than crop light [@vaverkova2026]. The clean annual-arable S1 case that the overstory geometry misses.

### Community-Solar Pollinator Array {#arch-community-solar}

[A3](1-the-scale-transect.qmd#sec-zones) · **[S3](2-the-sharingsparing-axis.qmd#sec-positions)** · *[management-led](1-the-scale-transect.qmd#sec-siting-latitude)*

*Dominant pressures:* [community acceptance](3-design-pressures.qmd#sec-pressures), [restorative goals](3-design-pressures.qmd#sec-pressures) with a pollinator/biodiversity service target, [grid and market demands](3-design-pressures.qmd#sec-pressures) (community-solar subscribers plus pollinator/habitat certification as the buying-side channel [@epri2021]).
*Yielded:* some [operations and maintenance](3-design-pressures.qmd#sec-pressures) during the multi-year establishment.
*Signature levers:* whole-site native [ground-layer](7-terminology.qmd#term-ground-layer) composition, seeded establishment, mowing/grazing timing set for bloom [@blaydes2022].

### Native-Grassland Utility Array {#arch-native-grassland}

[A4](1-the-scale-transect.qmd#sec-zones)–[A5](1-the-scale-transect.qmd#sec-zones) · **[S3](2-the-sharingsparing-axis.qmd#sec-positions)** · *[management-led](1-the-scale-transect.qmd#sec-siting-latitude)*

*Dominant pressures:* energy yield, restorative goals (grassland restoration [@walston2025]).
*Yielded:* agricultural production.
*Signature levers:* native seed mix, deferred/rotational mowing, soil-carbon establishment [@krasner2025; @carvalho2024]. The characteristic large-scale [convergence case](2-the-sharingsparing-axis.qmd#sec-wedge) (§2.2).

### Recharge Enhancement Array {#arch-recharge}

[A2](1-the-scale-transect.qmd#sec-zones)–[A3](1-the-scale-transect.qmd#sec-zones) · **[S4](2-the-sharingsparing-axis.qmd#sec-positions)** · *[siting-led](1-the-scale-transect.qmd#sec-siting-latitude)*

*Dominant pressures:* [restorative goals](3-design-pressures.qmd#sec-pressures) (a water-quantity target), [build cost](3-design-pressures.qmd#sec-pressures). What makes it pay is the [community & economic function](4-restorative-functions.qmd#sec-fn-community).
*Yielded:* some [energy yield](3-design-pressures.qmd#sec-pressures) (corners are small and awkwardly shaped).
*Signature levers:* placement on ground already out of production where infiltration can be increased, characteristically the dry corners a center-pivot never reaches, with ground-layer and grading chosen to move rainfall downward rather than off [@yavari2022]. The supply-side counterpart to [water-sustainability solar](#arch-water): where that one subtracts demand at scale, this one adds recharge on ground already out of production, and the pivot circle keeps farming beside it. **Emerging rather than established.** Kansas Geological Survey, Kansas State, and Michigan State researchers are testing the approach over the Ogallala; it is included as a named pathway to watch, not a documented recurring form.

### Linear Infrastructure Array {#arch-linear}

[A3](1-the-scale-transect.qmd#sec-zones)–[A4](1-the-scale-transect.qmd#sec-zones) · **[S4](2-the-sharingsparing-axis.qmd#sec-positions)** · *[siting-led](1-the-scale-transect.qmd#sec-siting-latitude)*

*Dominant pressures:* [build cost](3-design-pressures.qmd#sec-pressures) (land already disturbed and often already controlled), [community acceptance](3-design-pressures.qmd#sec-pressures) (prime fields left untouched).
*Yielded:* [energy yield](3-design-pressures.qmd#sec-pressures) and [operations and maintenance](3-design-pressures.qmd#sec-pressures), since a corridor is a costly shape to build and maintain.
*Signature levers:* placement along highway, rail, pipeline, and transmission easements; mounting specified for the wind and shadow conditions of a corridor; ground layer doubling as verge management. The geometry is the archetype: exceptionally long, narrow bands, so a strip a hundred feet wide and a mile long behaves nothing like a block of the same acreage. Its edge-to-area ratio is extreme, which is what makes it interesting for connectivity and hazardous for edge effects (see [influence zone](7-terminology.qmd#term-footprint-influence)), and it uses land already fragmented by the infrastructure beside it.

### Ag-Industrial Microgrid Array {#arch-microgrid}

[A3](1-the-scale-transect.qmd#sec-zones)–[A4](1-the-scale-transect.qmd#sec-zones) · **[S3](2-the-sharingsparing-axis.qmd#sec-positions)–[S4](2-the-sharingsparing-axis.qmd#sec-positions)** · *[siting-led](1-the-scale-transect.qmd#sec-siting-latitude)*

*Dominant pressures:* [grid and market demands](3-design-pressures.qmd#sec-pressures) in its purest form, since the load *is* the offtake, and farm economic resilience.
*Yielded:* [restorative goals](3-design-pressures.qmd#sec-pressures) on the ground layer, which is rarely the point at an industrial site.
*Signature levers:* siting against a heavy on-farm load such as grain drying, cold storage, a feedlot, or a processing complex, with battery storage sized to shave peaks, ride through outages, or arbitrage time-of-use rates. It is the one archetype organized around *when* power is used rather than what the ground does, and it is where the [community & economic function](4-restorative-functions.qmd#sec-fn-community) shows up as resilience rather than as rent.

### Brightfield / Reclaimed-Land Array {#arch-brightfield}

[A3](1-the-scale-transect.qmd#sec-zones)–[A5](1-the-scale-transect.qmd#sec-zones) · **[S4](2-the-sharingsparing-axis.qmd#sec-positions)** · *[siting-led](1-the-scale-transect.qmd#sec-siting-latitude)*

*Dominant pressures:* build cost (uniformly low-value ground), community acceptance (reuse of degraded land).
*Yielded:* some energy yield (sites are constrained).
*Signature levers:* placement on reclaimed mine land, landfills, and brownfields [@hernandez2019]; remediation constraints on foundations and ground layer. The standing [S4-at-A5 exception](2-the-sharingsparing-axis.qmd#sec-wedge) (§2.2).
